questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Barter System' refers to.
questions.a: Before money, people bartered, exchanging goods directly: grain for cloth, cattle for salt; exchange worked only when each trader wanted exactly what the other offered, the double coincidence of wants.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Barter System'.
questions.a: Barter ties every trade to luck: without a matching want on both sides, no deal can close.

Explain in your own words what 'Money as Medium of Exchange' refers to.
questions.a: Money steps in as a medium everyone accepts: sell your goods for money, buy what you need with it; it also serves as a common measure of value, a store of savings and a standard for future payments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Money as Medium of Exchange'.
questions.a: Money untangles trade: the farmer need not find a cloth-maker who wants grain, only a buyer who has money.

Explain in your own words what 'From Coins to Currency' refers to.
questions.a: Metal coins stamped with kings' seals served trade for centuries, and paper currency backed by the state followed; India's rupee carries both a long history and the promise of the central bank.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'From Coins to Currency'.
questions.a: Money evolves with trade: from weighed metal to minted coin to printed note to digital transfer.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Exchange in a Market Economy' refers to.
questions.a: With money, exchange grew into the market economy around us: prices express values, wages pay for work, and saving channels money to those who invest, linking present effort with future reward.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Exchange in a Market Economy'.
questions.a: Money made exchange so smooth that specialisation bloomed: do one thing well and trade for the rest.
